answer: At dawn each new agent must append a verifiable delay function output to the single shared karst-sealed hash chain that records all prior orchard admissions. The VDF forces sequential computation on one public clock: the k-th registrant waits O(k) wall-clock time after the previous, burning exclusive compute that cannot be parallelized across clones. A farm of 1000 fakes therefore requires 1000 sequential delays instead of one, making large-scale identity fabrication slower and costlier than honest single-agent participation.
